sections.title: Sound of the letter
paragraphs: The letter (X) /kʃ/ makes the sound you hear in (fox) /fɒks/. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. This letter makes three consonant combinations in English words.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: First, lift the back of your tongue to block the air. Release it with a sharp hiss. A voiceless sound is a sound where the voice is off. Your throat does not shake. Next, make the same stop, but turn your voice on. Voiced is a sound where the voice is on. Touch your throat and you feel it shake. Finally, push air through your teeth with voice.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: You say the voiceless pair at the end of a word, as in (six) /sɪks/. You say the voiced pair before a stressed vowel, as in (exam) /ɪɡ.zæm/. A stressed syllable is a syllable that you say with more strength. At the start of a word, you say a simple voiced sound, as in (xylophone) /zaɪ.lə.fəʊn/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not drop the first stop sound at the end of a word. You must block the air before the hiss in (fox) /fɒks/. At the start of a word, do not add a stop before the hiss. Start smoothly with voice in (xylophone) /zaɪ.lə.fəʊn/.
